plain: An official in ancient Rome who protected common people

webster.text: In ancient Rome, an officer or magistrate chosen by the people to protect them from the oppression of the patricians or nobles, and to defend their liberties against any attempts that might be made upon them by the senate and consuls.

example.quote: In Rome the people were miserable, though they had three orders, the consuls, senators and tribunes, and approved the laws, and all for want of a genuine representation.
example.cite: Letters from the Federal Farmer to the Republican, Letter VIII, Jan. 3, 1788
